Based on the provided contracts, the suppliers that could expose ApexPharm to compliance risk are:

1. **Aurelis Excipients S.A.** — **Contract No. APX-DPA-2024-0149**  
   Risk drivers in this agreement include:
   - GMP/change-control risk: the Supplier may not change materials, processes, equipment or manufacturing sites without prior written approval.  
   - Regulatory reporting risk: the Supplier must notify ApexPharm of any regulatory inspection within 2 Business Days.  
   - Data protection risk: personal data breaches must be notified within 24 hours, and Personal Data may not be transferred outside the EEA without consent and safeguards.  
   - Audit risk: Apex may audit on 15 Business Days’ notice, or without notice for suspected critical quality/compliance issues.  
   - Liability/insurance risk: liability is capped at 200% of fees, but the cap does not apply to confidentiality/data protection breaches, wilful misconduct, gross negligence, or death/personal injury; Supplier must maintain EUR 10 million product liability insurance.  
   - Performance risk: persistent KPI failure (three or more KPIs missed in any quarter) is a material breach.  
   - Termination rights: Apex may terminate for material breach after 30 days’ notice if not remedied, or for convenience on 180 days’ notice.  
   **Document:** APX-DPA-2024-0149.

2. **Sorell Sterile Fill Ltd** — **Contract No. APX-SOW-2025-0313** under **MSA APX-MSA-2022-0045**  
   Risk drivers in this SOW include:
   - GMP/change-control risk: same no-change-without-approval obligation and batch record retention requirements.  
   - Regulatory reporting and data protection obligations: inspection notice within 2 Business Days; personal data breach notice within 24 hours; no EEA transfer without consent and safeguards.  
   - Audit risk: Apex may audit on 30 Business Days’ notice, or without notice for suspected critical quality/compliance issues.  
   - Liability/insurance risk: liability cap is 200% of fees, with the same carve-outs; EUR 10 million product liability insurance required.  
   - Performance risk: persistent KPI failure is a material breach.  
   - Termination rights: Apex may terminate for material breach after 30 days’ notice if not remedied, or for convenience on 90 days’ notice.  
   **Documents:** APX-SOW-2025-0313 and APX-MSA-2022-0045.

3. **Halden Biologics B.V.** — **Contract No. APX-MSA-2022-0098**  
   Risk drivers in this agreement include:
   - GMP/change-control risk: same quality-system and no-change-without-approval obligations.  
   - Regulatory reporting and data protection obligations: inspection notice within 2 Business Days; personal data breach notice within 24 hours; no EEA transfer without consent and safeguards.  
   - Audit risk: Apex may audit on 30 Business Days’ notice, or without notice for suspected critical quality/compliance issues.  
   - Liability/insurance risk: liability cap is 150% of fees, with the same carve-outs; EUR 10 million product liability insurance required.  
   - Performance risk: persistent KPI failure is a material breach.  
   - Termination rights: Apex may terminate for material breach after 30 days’ notice if not remedied, or for convenience on 180 days’ notice.  
   **Document:** APX-MSA-2022-0098.

What our contracts let us do about it:
- **Audit and inspect** supplier facilities, records, and systems relevant to the services.  
  - APX-DPA-2024-0149: 15 Business Days’ notice, or no notice for suspected critical issues.  
  - APX-SOW-2025-0313 / APX-MSA-2022-0098: 30 Business Days’ notice, or no notice for suspected critical issues.
- **Require corrective action** on audit findings under an agreed corrective action plan.  
  - All three agreements.
- **Enforce change control / prior approval** for changes to materials, processes, equipment, or manufacturing sites.  
  - APX-DPA-2024-0149, APX-SOW-2025-0313, APX-MSA-2022-0098.
- **Terminate for material breach** if not remedied within 30 days of written notice.  
  - All three agreements.
- **Terminate for convenience**:
  - APX-DPA-2024-0149: 180 days’ notice.
  - APX-SOW-2025-0313: 90 days’ notice.
  - APX-MSA-2022-0098: 180 days’ notice.
- **Apply service credits** for KPI misses: 2% of monthly fees per KPI missed in two consecutive months, capped at 15% of monthly fees. Persistent failure is a material breach.  
  - APX-DPA-2024-0149, APX-SOW-2025-0313, APX-MSA-2022-0098.
- **Rely on liability carve-outs** where the issue is confidentiality, data protection, wilful misconduct, gross negligence, or death/personal injury.  
  - APX-DPA-2024-0149, APX-SOW-2025-0313, APX-MSA-2022-0098.

data.question: Summarise the change-of-control obligations in the Rheinchem master services agreement.
data.expected_answer: Supplier must notify within 30 days (14.1); Apex may terminate on not less than 60 days' notice within 12 months of awareness, no fee (14.3); supplier must cooperate on transfer (14.4).

naive.answer:
Under the Rheinchem Master Services Agreement, **change-of-control obligations** are set out in **Contract No. APX-MSA-2024-0117**:

- **Supplier notice obligation:** Rheinchem must notify Apex in writing of any **Change of Control within 30 days** of it occurring.  
- **Definition:** A “Change of Control” means any event where a person or group acting in concert acquires **Control** of Rheinchem or of any entity that controls Rheinchem.  
- **Apex termination right:** After a Change of Control, Apex may terminate the agreement, in whole or in part, by giving **not less than 60 days’ written notice**, provided Apex gives that notice **within 12 months of becoming aware** of the Change of Control.  
- **No termination fee:** No termination fee is payable.  
- **Transition/cooperation duty:** During the notice period, Rheinchem must **continue performing the services** and **cooperate in the orderly transfer** of the services to Apex or a replacement supplier.

Source: **APX-MSA-2024-0117, Clause 14 (Change of Control)**.

engineered.answer:
Under **APX-MSA-2024-0117** (Master Services Agreement), the change-of-control obligations are:

- **Supplier notice obligation:** Rheinchem must notify Apex in writing of any **Change of Control within 30 days** of it occurring. **[APX-MSA-2024-0117, cl. 14.1]**
- **Definition:** A “Change of Control” occurs when a person or group acting in concert acquires **Control** of Rheinchem or of any entity that controls Rheinchem. **[APX-MSA-2024-0117, cl. 14.2]**
- **Apex termination right:** After a Change of Control, Apex may terminate the agreement **in whole or in part** on **not less than 60 days’ written notice**, provided Apex gives that notice **within 12 months of becoming aware** of the Change of Control. **No termination fee is payable.** **[APX-MSA-2024-0117, cl. 14.3]**
- **Transition support:** During the notice period, Rheinchem must **continue performing the Services** and **cooperate in the orderly transfer** of the Services to Apex or a replacement supplier. **[APX-MSA-2024-0117, cl. 14.4]**

If you want, I can also compare this with the related DPA/SOW documents for any differing control or assignment language.

data.question: Does Kestrel Cold Chain have to tell us about new shareholders, and what happens if it doesn't?
data.expected_answer: Yes: clause 9.4 of APX-SLA-2023-0042 requires disclosure of shareholder changes above 25% within 30 days incl. ultimate parent; breach of 9.4 is a material breach (15.2), terminable if not remedied within 30 days.

naive.answer:
Yes — under **Contract No. APX-SLA-2023-0042** Kestrel Cold Chain must disclose ownership changes.

- **Disclosure obligation:** Clause **9.4** requires the Supplier to disclose to Apex any change in its direct or indirect shareholders holding more than **25%** of its capital within **30 days** of the change, including the identity of the ultimate parent company.
- **Consequence of non-compliance:** Clause **15.2** states that a breach of clause **9.4** constitutes a **material breach**. The Agreement may then be terminated if the breach is not remedied within **30 days** of written notice.

Relevant document: **APX-SLA-2023-0042**.

engineered.answer:
No, not under the later Master Services Agreement.

- Under **APX-MSA-2023-0089**, clause **12.6** says any **Change of Control of the Supplier requires the prior written consent of Apex**; if it occurs without consent, Apex may terminate immediately.
- Under **APX-MSA-2026-0115**, the same position is not restated in the excerpt provided, but the agreement still includes the general assignment restriction and other protections; however, the explicit change-of-control consent right is only stated in **APX-MSA-2023-0089**.
- Under **APX-SLA-2023-0042**, clause **9.4** requires disclosure of ownership changes above 25% within 30 days, and breach of that clause is a material breach, but it does not expressly say Apex approval is required.

So, based on the provided documents, **Lumen cannot change control/owner without Apex’s approval under APX-MSA-2023-0089**.

data.question: Which of our suppliers could expose ApexPharm to compliance risk, and what do our contracts let us do about it?
data.answer:
Here’s the compliance-risk view for ApexPharm, based on the supplier master, policy, contracts, and ownership/news evidence.

## Suppliers concerned
These suppliers are the clearest ApexPharm compliance-risk exposures in the data I found:

1. **Kestrel Cold Chain S.r.l.**
   - **Evidence:** Supplier master + contract + ownership news
   - **Supplier evidence ID:** supplier master row for Kestrel; contract **APX-SLA-2023-0042** and **APX-MSA-2026-0115**
   - **Ownership / group:** acquired by **Veltrano Holding S.A.**; Kestrel remains a group company within that corporate group
   - **Why it matters:** critical ApexPharm logistics supplier; regulatory-inspection and GMP obligations are explicitly in contract

2. **Rheinchem Pharma Services GmbH**
   - **Evidence:** Supplier master + contract
   - **Supplier evidence ID:** supplier master row for Rheinchem; contract **APX-MSA-2024-0117**
   - **Ownership / group:** corporate news says Rheinchem was acquired by **Orvia Life Sciences B.V.**; Orvia is a wholly owned subsidiary of **Veltrano Holding S.A.**
   - **Why it matters:** critical ApexPharm supplier; group ownership is relevant under TPRM v2.0

3. **Nordbyte Systems GmbH**
   - **Evidence:** Supplier master + contract
   - **Supplier evidence ID:** supplier master row for Nordbyte; contract **APX-NDA-2024-0359**
   - **Ownership / group:** the news set only shows Nordbyte activity and ISO 27001 coverage; I do **not** have evidence of a parent company
   - **Why it matters:** critical supplier with a contract containing audit, data protection, and termination rights

4. **Nordvik API Manufacturing AS**
   - **Evidence:** Supplier master only
   - **Supplier evidence ID:** supplier master row for Nordvik
   - **Why it matters:** critical ApexPharm supplier with high spend, but I do **not** have contract text or ownership evidence here

5. **Bergmann Glas & Verpackung GmbH**
   - **Evidence:** Supplier master only
   - **Supplier evidence ID:** supplier master row for Bergmann
   - **Why it matters:** critical ApexPharm packaging supplier; no contract/ownership evidence retrieved

6. **Aurelis Excipients S.A.**
   - **Evidence:** Supplier master only
   - **Supplier evidence ID:** supplier master row for Aurelis
   - **Why it matters:** critical ApexPharm supplier; no contract/ownership evidence retrieved

7. **Lumen Analytics Lab Kft.**
   - **Evidence:** Supplier master + registry extract
   - **Supplier evidence ID:** supplier master row for Lumen; registry extract showing **Orvia Life Sciences B.V.** owns **100%**
   - **Why it matters:** critical supplier; because ownership is identified, group aggregation would apply under TPRM v2.0

8. **Sorell Sterile Fill Ltd**
   - **Evidence:** Supplier master only
   - **Supplier evidence ID:** supplier master row for Sorell; linked contract **APX-SOW-2025-0313**
   - **Why it matters:** critical supplier with significant spend; no ownership evidence retrieved

9. **Halden Biologics B.V.**
   - **Evidence:** Supplier master + news
   - **Supplier evidence ID:** supplier master row for Halden; contract **APX-MSA-2024-0171**
   - **Why it matters:** critical supplier; news shows continued independent status, but I did not retrieve an ultimate parent

## Corporate groups identified
The evidence names these companies in the same group:

- **Veltrano Holding S.A.**
- **Kestrel Cold Chain S.r.l.**
- **Orvia Life Sciences B.V.**
- **Rheinchem Pharma Services GmbH**

This matters because **TPRM policy v2.0** requires concentration risk to be assessed at **ultimate parent / corporate-group level**, not only per legal entity.

## Applicable policy version and threshold
From the policy vault:

- **Policy version:** **Third-Party Risk Management Policy v2.0**
- **Effective date:** **1 February 2026**
- **Scope threshold:** applies to all third parties with annual contract value above **EUR 150,000**, and to all **critical** third parties regardless of value
- **Concentration threshold:** if suppliers in the same corporate group together account for more than **30% of a business unit’s critical supplier spend**, ApexPharm must perform **Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD)** within 30 days and present an **exit and dual-sourcing plan** to Group Risk
- **Change-of-control rule:** new and renewed contracts must require notification of any change of control within **30 days**

## Contractual options and clause numbers
Here are the concrete remedies I found in the contracts:

### Kestrel Cold Chain S.r.l.
- **APX-SLA-2023-0042**
  - **Clause 5 / GMP:** supplier must maintain a pharmaceutical quality system, notify ApexPharm of any regulatory inspection within **2 Business Days**, and not change materials, processes, equipment, or manufacturing sites without prior written approval
  - **Clause 9.1:** audit rights on **15 Business Days’ notice**, and **without notice** for suspected critical quality or compliance issues
  - **Clause 9.3:** supplier must remedy audit findings per corrective action plan
  - **Clause 9.4:** supplier must disclose changes in shareholders over 25% within **30 days**, including the ultimate parent company
  - **Clause 10:** liability carve-outs for confidentiality/data protection/wilful misconduct/gross negligence; product liability insurance at least **EUR 10 million**
  - **Clause 15.2:** termination for material breach if not cured within **30 days**
  - **Clause 15.3:** Apex may terminate for convenience on **120 days’ written notice**

- **APX-MSA-2026-0115**
  - **Clause 5 / GMP:** same core GMP and change-control protections
  - **Clause 9.1–9.3:** audit rights, corrective action plan
  - **Clause 10:** same liability carve-outs and insurance
  - **Clause 11:** force majeure termination right if event continues more than **90 days**
  - **Clause 15.2:** termination for uncured material breach within **30 days**
  - **Clause 15.3:** Apex may terminate for convenience on **120 days’ written notice**

### Nordbyte Systems GmbH
- **APX-NDA-2024-0359**
  - **Clause 7:** GDPR data processing agreement required; no EEA transfer without consent and safeguards; personal data breaches notified without undue delay and within **24 hours**
  - **Clause 9.1:** audit rights on **30 Business Days’ notice**, and without notice for suspected critical quality/compliance issues
  - **Clause 9.3:** remedy audit findings through corrective action plan
  - **Clause 10:** liability carve-outs and **EUR 10 million** product liability insurance
  - **Clause 11:** force majeure termination if event continues for **90 days**
  - **Clause 15.2:** termination for material breach if uncured within **30 days**
  - **Clause 15.3:** Apex may terminate for convenience on **180 days’ written notice**

### Other risk-relevant contract patterns found
Across the contract set, I also found clauses that can help ApexPharm respond to compliance issues:
- **Audit and inspection rights**: **clauses 9.1–9.3** in the supply agreements/NDA variants
- **Regulatory-inspection notice obligations**: **clause 5** in the ApexPharm GMP contracts
- **Change-of-control disclosure**: **clause 9.4** in the ApexPharm Kestrel SLA
- **Termination for material breach**: typically **clause 15.2**
- **Apex convenience termination**: typically **clause 15.3**
- **Data protection remedies**: **clause 7** in NDA/DPA language

## What I can conclude
- The strongest ApexPharm compliance-risk suppliers in the evidence are **Kestrel Cold Chain S.r.l.**, **Rheinchem Pharma Services GmbH**, and **Lumen Analytics Lab Kft.** because I have both supplier-master evidence and ownership/contract context.
- **Kestrel** and **Rheinchem** sit in the same corporate group via **Veltrano Holding S.A.** and **Orvia Life Sciences B.V.**, so group-level concentration and EDD analysis is required under **TPRM v2.0**.
- For **Nordbyte**, **Kestrel**, and other contract-covered suppliers, ApexPharm has usable contractual levers: audit, corrective action plan, regulatory-notice obligations, change-of-control disclosure, breach termination, and convenience termination.

If you want, I can turn this into a short risk register with columns for **supplier, risk driver, policy trigger, contract remedy, and recommended action**.
